title: Specification
body:
A Specification details the requirements for determining whether a network unduly burdens its beneficiaries (members or employees) with regard to access to care from in-network providers by ensuring beneficiaries have access to sufficient numbers of providers based on their specialties, travel time, and distance. Specifications are part of the criteria when performing an Accessibility or Adequacy analysis. Thus, depending on your selected criteria and whether your project is enabled for both Accessibility and Adequacy, you may use the same specification in either module. CMS Medicare Advantage Specifications are available within the Adequacy and Accessibility modules for the most recent years when you use the Standard CMS Medicare Advantage specialty mapping. These are found in the subcategory Global Specifications and are not editable.

Adding a New Specification

 A new specification can be added from four different places within Network360. * Go to **My Things** on the left side bar navigation menu: * Select **My Specifications** * Click on the **+Add New** link * Go to **Compliance** on the left side bar navigation menu: * Select **Specifications** * Click on the **+Add New Specification** button. * Within the **Accessibility** module: * Click on the **+Add New Analysis** button * Click on the **+Add New Specification** link * Within the **Adequacy** module: * Click on the **+Add New Analysis** button * Click on the **+Add Adequacy Specification** button. On the **Create New Specification** page: 1. Enter a unique **Name** for your specification. 2. To share with other users, click the **Share with everyone in your organization** checkbox. 3. Select a **Specialty Mapping** from the dropdown list. 4. Select an **Area Type**: * **CBSA** (Core-Based Statistical Areas) is a county type classification defined by the US Office of Management and Budget based on the most recently available US Census Bureau population estimates and density parameter. CBSA is divided into the following categories: * Large Metro * Metro * Micro * Rural * CEAC (Counties with Extreme Access)  * **USR** (Urban-Suburban-Rural) categorizes zip codes based on their residential population size per square mile. USR is divided into the following categories: * Urban * Suburban * Rural 5. Select a **Distance Type** - This is the method of measuring distance between the member and provider. * **Estimated Driving Distance** is the approximate undirected driving distance from the zip+4 centroid (Point A) to the specific provider (Point B). * **Straight-line Distance** is the shortest distance from the zip+4 centroid (Point A) to the specific provider (Point B). This is also known as “As the crow flies.” **Note:** **Available Reports** are based on Area Type and Distance Type selections, as indicated on the left side of the page. Once all selections have been made, click on the **Next** button to save these selections as the general properties of your specification.

Standards

 You can create and customize the standards by which Accessibility and Adequacy are determined. Regulatory minimum count and mileage standards for a given provider type or specialty usually vary depending on the population density of the area where members are located. When the **Show Accessibility Criteria Only** field is set to **No**, you can determine the **Minimum Success %** for each **Region Type** (e.g. Rural) by typing your desired benchmark in the category’s field or using the arrows to make your selection. The minimum success % and minimum provider ratio (per 1000 members) are useful benchmarks for Adequacy analyses. Click the **Save** button in the bottom right corner to make the adequacy specification available for use. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/standards.png) In this section, you can also edit, delete, or add new standards. The standards are listed by provider type or specialty group with the specifics for each population density classification type. ### Edit a Standard 1. Click the edit icon on the right-most column within the table for the provider type. 2. Change the desired selections for minimum provider ratio, minimum number of providers, and miles/minutes distance for each geographic category. 3. Click the save icon on the right-most column within the table to save your changes. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/editstandards.png) ### Delete a Standard 1. For the provider type which you want to delete, click the delete icon in the right-most column within the table. 2. In the pop-up confirmation message click on Yes. ### Add a Standard 1. In the bottom, right corner of the **Standards** table, click on the **Add Standard** button. 2. In the specialty field, select either a provider type or specialty group. 3. Make your desired selections for minimum provider ratio, minimum number of providers, and miles/minutes distance for each geographic category. 4. Click the save icon on the right-most column within the table to save the new standard. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/addstandards.png)
